reviews.body:
Thanks for your submission, I'll will probably take a look at handling `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` content block instead of silently dropping them. 

We should probably have an option in the settings for ignoring unsupported content blocks.

comments.body:
The workflow runs are sitting in `action_required` (first-time-contributor gate) — could someone "Approve and run workflows"?

Local verification while it's waiting:

```
$ make format && make check-format
uv run ruff format .        → 369 files left unchanged
uv run ruff check --fix .   → All checks passed!
uv run ruff format --check . → 369 files already formatted

$ make test-unit PACKAGE=giskard-llm
238 selected, 231 passed, 7 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed

$ pre-commit run --all-files   (on the changed files, via git commit)
ruff check ............................................ Passed
ruff format ............................................ Passed
basedpyright ............................................ Passed
Detect secrets .......................................... Passed
```

The four new tests in `test_anthropic_chat_return.py` were confirmed to fail on the unpatched code (reverted the fix locally, reran — 3 `ValueError: Unsupported content block type` failures, 1 pass) before confirming green with the fix.

Thanks @kevinmessiaen, agreed that silently dropping them isn't ideal. Before I rework this, I'd like to check the shape you have in mind:

1. **Thinking blocks:** add a `ThinkingContent` (thinking text + `signature`, plus a redacted variant) to `CompletionContent`, and exclude it from `.text` so chain-of-thought never ends up in what Equals/Contains/LLM judges evaluate. Keeping the signature would also let a thinking + tool-use turn be sent back to Anthropic unchanged.
2. **Other unmapped blocks** (`server_tool_use`, `web_search_tool_result`, …): a setting like `ignore_unsupported_content_blocks`. Should it default to `False` (keep raising) or `True`?

For context, #2843 reports that Claude 5 models emit `thinking` blocks by default, so this currently breaks any check run against them. Happy to fold this into #2830 or close it in favour of whichever direction you prefer.

Hey, sorry for the slow reply, and thanks for taking the time to sketch this out. What you proposed is pretty close to where we ended up.

On your two questions:

1. We're not going to add a new content type for thinking. We'd rather stick to what the OpenAI-compatible ecosystem already does (OpenRouter, vLLM, DeepSeek), so `AssistantMessage` gets a `reasoning: str | None` field (accepting `reasoning_content` as an alias) plus `reasoning_details`, a list of `reasoning.text` (with `signature`), `reasoning.summary` and `reasoning.encrypted` items. Neither one ends up in `.text`, so checks only ever see the actual answer.
2. For blocks we can't map, the default is to raise a dedicated `UnsupportedContentError`. There'll be a provider option, `ignore_unsupported_content=True`, for people who'd rather drop them, and it logs a warning when it does.

We'll do the shared types and the option ourselves since they touch every provider, and should have a PR up soon. Once that's merged, would you be up for reworking this one on top of it? Roughly:
- `thinking` → a `reasoning.text` detail with its signature (`format="anthropic-claude-v1"`)
- `redacted_thinking` → `reasoning.encrypted`
- serializing them back as the leading thinking blocks on assistant turns, so tool-use turns keep working when thinking is enabled

Your existing tests should mostly carry over. Since Claude 5 is affected by default we can't sit on it for too long, so if we haven't heard from you about a week after the base PR lands, we'll pick it up ourselves. No pressure either way!

Thanks, that shape makes sense. Happy to rework this on top of your base PR once it lands: thinking → `reasoning.text` with signature (`anthropic-claude-v1`), redacted_thinking → `reasoning.encrypted`, and round-tripping them as leading blocks on assistant turns. Ping me when it's up.

@kevinmessiaen The rework is ready on top of #2867, as one commit on its current head (475b873): https://github.com/pcbeingused333/giskard-oss/compare/Giskard-AI:claude/giskard-llm-reasoning-content-c5495a...pcbeingused333:anthropic-thinking-v2

- `thinking` becomes a `reasoning.text` detail with its `signature`, and `redacted_thinking` becomes a `reasoning.encrypted` detail, both with `format="anthropic-claude-v1"`. The thinking text is also exposed as `reasoning`. Neither ends up in `content`, so `.text` stays the answer.
- On assistant turns, Anthropic-format details are serialized back as the leading `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` blocks, so tool use keeps working with thinking enabled. Unsigned text, summaries and other providers' reasoning are skipped, since Anthropic verifies the signature.
- The unsupported-content tests now use `server_tool_use`, which is still unmapped.

`make test-unit PACKAGE=giskard-llm` (278 passed, 7 skipped), ruff and basedpyright are clean, with the same 52 pre-existing warnings in `anthropic.py`. Once #2867 lands I'll move it onto `main` and update this PR, or open a new one if you prefer.
@pcbeingused333 thanks, we will take a look at your contribution!
Closing this one: #2888 fixed the same crash on Anthropic thinking blocks upstream, so it's no longer needed. Thanks!
